done.why: I lost track of the princess after she woke and walked off. She was clearly the 'lady' the unicorn's key was waiting for, and that key opens the Wizard's door. I waited at the unicorn and she never came. My lamp was dimming, I was near 270 turns, and the only other open thread was the Bank, which looked like a whole new puzzle. So I stopped.

about: A sly, prank-playing Wizard has carried off the Empire's treasures and scattered them through caverns south of a ravine. You go after them: a riddle door, a well you ride up in a bucket, an Alice-in-Wonderland tea room, a spinning room you have to switch off, a baseball diamond made of glassy rooms, and a dragon you trick into fighting his own reflection. Meanwhile the Wizard keeps popping in to cast half-finished spells on you.

moments.note: The Wizard sizes me up and hints at the goal: pearls behind a door that asks a question, and a room that won't keep still. That gave me a purpose right away.
The 'convention of wizards' was an illusion from his 'Fantasize!' spell. The room 'has the grace to look embarrassed'.
The unicorn's key is tied in a bow meant for 'somebody in particular, a lady'. A clear signal I wasn't the one to take it.
"a well" got a hollow laugh. Plain "well" worked.
Examining the bucket told me exactly what to do (fresh water from the ford, carried in the teapot) without just handing me the answer.
Oddly-angled room: whether a direction counted depended on which room I was in. 'Lost count' kept showing up while the window still flickered, and that was hard to read.
Ran the bases (N, SE, NE, NW) and the window glowed brightly. Working out the baseball diamond felt great.
Going one more step after home gave a 'rusty squeal' far off, and a secret passage opened to Cerberus.
While it was spinning, the carousel kept dropping me in the Cool Room when I wanted the Riddle Room. A lot of turns went on retrying.
Three attacks in one room and the dragon incinerated me. I hadn't been warned that a third hit there would be fatal.
Death took me into the misty crystal sphere and a horrible imprisoned face, which sent me back. Nice, though my gear got scattered.
Poured the water into the bucket and rode it up to the Top of Well. 'Well done.'
Read the tiny cake letters through the glass flask and got 'Evaporate'. Very satisfying.
Had the robot push the triangular button and the carousel stopped. A steel box with the violin had fallen into it.
The lizard wolfed down the candies. 'It seemed to enjoy the grasshoppers particularly.'
The dragon saw himself in the ice and melted it, which killed him. The lamp-reflection hint finally paid off.
The princess walked south while I fiddled with the chest, and I never found her again.

wished: Follow the princess, or ask where she went, after she left the lair
Stop the carousel without such a long detour, or at least steer it while it spun
Get a clearer warning that a third attack on the dragon in one room would kill me
Carry the violin. My load was too heavy, and I couldn't easily tell what to drop
Have "a well" accepted as an answer, not only "well"

lines.line: It is all south of the ravine, his look says, every treasure the Empire mislaid, and much good may it do you; the pearls nearest, behind a stone door that asks a question
lines.why: It set my goal and pointed me somewhere without spoiling it.

lines.line: the room, having no say in the matter, let it, and has the grace to look embarrassed about it now.
lines.why: A funny, characterful way to show that the Wizard's spells are fakes.

lines.line: It will wait for her. You need not.
lines.why: It told me plainly to leave the key for later and set up the princess.

lines.line: Whatever it is that makes it go up, it will go up with what is in it and without what is not; that is the whole art of buckets.
lines.why: A hint that was also a nice line.

lines.line: he has caught sight of himself in the polished brass of your lamp, and that he does not care for the look of the other dragon in it at all.
lines.why: The key clue to the dragon. It clicked once I saw the ice.

lines.line: Dragons are smart, but sometimes naive, and this one has never seen ice before.
lines.why: My reward for the hardest puzzle I solved.

fun.why: Solving the bucket, the cakes, the bases and the dragon each felt great. The spinning carousel's random rerouting and losing the princess took some of the fun away.

engagement.why: The Wizard's opening hint gave me a goal at once, and every puzzle I solved opened new ground, so I kept wanting to push on. Engagement dropped while I ground through carousel retries.

difficulty.why: The hints were fair: the bucket description, the lamp reflection, the scoreboard window. But the oddly-angled room was opaque, the dragon killed me without warning, and the carousel was random, so it leaned hard.

interestingness.why: The places were varied and inventive: a baseball-diamond maze, the Alice tea room, a robot and a machine room, a dragon beaten by his reflection, and an afterlife inside a crystal sphere.

prose.why: Wry and well paced, with rooms that 'look embarrassed', the 'whole art of buckets', and candy eaten 'including the package'. Even the hints read as prose rather than instructions.
